description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative: The humanitarian response in Sudan is severely underfunded, resulting in needs reaching catastrophic levels. South Darfur (SD) hosts 18% (1,812,264) of Sudan's total internally displaced persons (IDPs) with limited humanitarian aid; 95% of IDPs need food, 60% require livelihood support, and 40% need nutrition assistance (IOM, 2024). The June 2024 Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report shows a rapid deterioration in food security across Sudan. The situation in SD (with Nyala in IPC4) is expected to worsen over the next 2 quarters, with 36% of the population projected to be in emergency (IPC4) and catastrophic (IPC5) phases. The Sudan Famine Prevention Plan and the FSL cluster identified a need for cash for food, to enable affected hard-to-reach communities avert famine and prevent negative coping mechanisms (selling of assets, reducing the number and portion size of meals, which has severe bearing on nutrition and Dietary Diversity Score, especially among children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW)). The Sudan Nutrition Cluster classifies SD as a high-priority area for nutrition, with 137,497 individuals needing nutrition assistance in Nyala alone (87,053 in Nyala Shimal; 50,444 in Nyala Janoub) and significant gaps in service delivery. CARE’s latest Rapid Gender Analysis (RGA) indicates cash as top priority (57%), linked to the loss of income. Female-headed households (HH) are more vulnerable to food insecurity (42%) compared to male-headed HH (31%) and have a 10% lower food intake. In response to critical needs and gaps, in line with Cluster/Working Group recommendations, CARE and SUDO propose an integrated lifesaving FSL and nutrition intervention. The project, which mainstreams protection, is designed to complement partners’ ongoing programmes targeting the population affected by ongoing conflict, (IDPs and the host community) in Nyala, SD. Synergies with health and nutrition services increase the lifesaving potential of cash assistance.

title.narrative: Number of people enabled to meet their basic food needs

comment.narrative: A total of 341 families were registered, verified, and received three rounds of multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA). Among them, 151 families had malnutrition cases referred from nutrition centers, 6 were SGBV cases, and 7 were acute health cases referred from health facilities. Additionally, 177 vulnerable families, including women-headed households, newly displaced individuals, and households with persons with disabilities and the elderly, also benefited from the assistance.

A total of 70 community nutrition volunteers were trained and involved in delivering nutrition services, ensuring the program reached the most vulnerable populations. Additionally, 50 members of the Community Cash Distribution Committee played a vital role in community mobilization and the registration of vulnerable families targeted for cash assistance.

title.narrative: Number of children under 5 admitted for treatment of Severe or Moderate Acute Malnutrition

comment.narrative: Actual comment A total of 2,993 children under five were admitted to the nutrition program, including 1,052 cases of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and 1,941 cases of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). SAM cases without medical complications were admitted to four nutrition centers established and supported by this program: Al Jabal, Al Wehda West, and Al Wadi West in Nyala Janoub locality, and Al Nahda nutrition center in Nyala Shamal locality of South Darfur State.

SUDO, with the support of CARE and in collaboration with SMoH - South Darfur, established services and supported the operation of four nutrition centers (Alwadi Kharb, Alwehda Kharb, and Aljabal nutrition centers in Nyala Janoub, and Alnahada nutrition center in Nyala Shamala locality in Nyala Shamal of South Darfur state).

title.narrative: Number of people screened for under nutrition

comment.narrative: During the reporting period, 19,632 children under five (10,091 females and 9,541 males) were screened for malnutrition by trained community nutrition volunteers. Of these, 859 were admitted to the nutrition program for further support.As part of the ongoing mass MUAC screening campaign, SUDO and CARE aim to reach an additional 13,000 children under five with malnutrition screening and nutritional education, ensuring early detection and intervention to improve child health outcomes.

SUDO provided training to 70 nutrition volunteers, 60 community volunteers, and 40 lead mothers on Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) screening. Throughout the project, MUAC screening reached a total of 23,100 individuals. This included females and males under 18 years of age, women above 18, and individuals with disabilities across different age groups. SUDO trained 40 lead mothers in the Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) approach. These trained mothers then screened and established 10 mother support groups, each consisting of 10 pregnant and lactating women with moderate malnutrition identified within their communities.

title.narrative: "Are two or more partners carrying out joint programming in one geographical areas within the JR? YES/NO"

comment.narrative: Four partners ( CARE, SUDO, ZOA and GFO) are operating in the same geographical areas of Nyala Janoub and Nyala Shamal. To enhance coordination and efficiency, a coordination platform was established, ensuring clear demarcation of sub-locations for each partner. This has effectively prevented overlaps and duplication of activities.A monthly coordination forum has been set up, with regular meetings held to strengthen collaboration and information sharing among partners.

title.narrative: Percentage of budget spent on capacity building of national and local actors

comment.narrative: A total of €22,107.50 (5% of the total project budget) was allocated for the capacity building of local partners and actors. An assessment was conducted to identify specific capacity-building needs, revealing a demand for training in project development, proposal and report writing, and project cycle management, which has since been completed.

The initial plan for partner capacity building was 5% of the budget €22,107.50. However, due to the ongoing conflict, staff turnover at the partner level remained high. As a result, additional staff had to be trained to ensure sufficient capacity to deliver the project with acceptable quality and within the planned timelines.
